curl -H "x-apikey: db_key456" \\\n https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/dropbox.com/threat-actors
``` | | **6. Parse the JSON response** | The response will contain a list of threat‑actor objects. Look for fields like `name`, `description`, `aliases`, etc. | ```json
{
"data": [
{

Check the `links` section for `next` URLs. - **Rate Limits**: VirusTotal free tier allows ~4 requests/minute. If you hit limits, wait or upgrade. - **Data Fields**: Besides `name` and `description`, you might find `first_seen`, `last_seen`, and `related_entities`. ### Example Python Snippet If you prefer Python, here’s a minimal example using `requests`: ```python import requests API_KEY = "db_key456" DOMAIN = "dropbox.com" URL = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}/threat-actors" headers = {"x-apikey": API_KEY} response = requests.get(URL, headers=headers) if response.status_code == 200: data = response.json() for actor in data.get("data", []): attrs = actor.get("attributes", {}) print(f"Name: {attrs.get('name')}") print(f"Description: {attrs.get('description')}") print(f"Aliases: {', '.join(attrs.get('aliases', []))}\n") else: print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}") ``` Feel free to adapt the code to your environment.
